notes_list.title: Williamson Ether Synthesis
notes_list.basic_overview: An alkoxide ion reacts with an alkyl halide or sulfonate through an SN2 pathway to form an ether.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
Best substrates for the electrophile are primary alkyl halides. Secondary substrates may compete with elimination, while tertiary alkyl halides generally favor elimination rather than clean SN2 substitution. Example: CH3CH2ONa + CH3I → CH3CH2OCH3.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
An alkoxide attacks a primary alkyl electrophile by SN2, displacing the leaving group and forming the ether.
